Hello! I am **Wei Wang**, a Ph.D. Candidate in Learning Design and Technology at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, and a co-founder of **AskAboutEdu (askabout.edu)**. I study how generative AI, learning analytics, and evidence-grounded systems can support teaching, learning, critical thinking, AI literacy, and educational decision-making.

My work combines design-based research, mixed methods, and computational analysis. I build and evaluate tools ranging from retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems to interactive educational data platforms, using Python, R, natural language processing, and causal inference methods.

## Research focus

- Generative AI, critical thinking, and AI literacy in teaching and learning
- Learning analytics, educational data mining, and computational research methods
- Evidence-informed decision support and evaluation of educational technologies

## Recent work

- First author of an [**accepted JEDM article on LLM-assisted educational video transcript analysis**](Publications/Educational_Video_Transcript_LLMs/JEDM_Article.qmd).
- Co-editing [***[AI and Me] Generative AI Guidebook for Higher Education Faculty***](Publications/AI_and_Me_Guidebook/Guidebook.qmd), currently awaiting administrator review in the EdTech Books open publishing system.
- Co-founding [**AskAboutEdu**](Projects/Ask_About_EDU/Ask_About_EDU.qmd) and developing reproducible RAG workflows that connect practical education questions with traceable research evidence.
- Co-leading the UTK ORIED-funded [**Next Level Teaching Blueprint**](Projects/Next_Level_Teaching_Blueprint/Next_Level_Teaching_Blueprint.qmd) as Student PI and Graduate Researcher, examining how constraint-first, dialogic AI activities can strengthen critical thinking in research methods courses.
- Leading the forthcoming CRC Press book [*Computational Analysis of Educational Data: A Field Guide Using R*](Publications/Computational_Analysis_Educational_Data/Book.qmd) as first author (expected late 2026).
- Co-developing the [**AIREA Data Explorer**](Projects/CCRC_Green_Seek_Mapping%20Project/GreenSeek.qmd), a public tool linking community college credentials and regional workforce demand.
- Contributing to [**preprints and manuscripts in progress**](Publications.qmd) on AI curriculum materials, causal sensitivity analysis, faculty GenAI literacy, international students' online learning, and changing data science work.

## Teaching and professional background

Since August 2023, I have worked as a Teaching Assistant and Research Assistant with **UTK Digital Learning**, supporting research on AI-enhanced online teaching and faculty development. My teaching experience includes [**ESM 250: Applied Statistical Concepts for Decision Makers**](Teaching/ESM_250/ESM_250.qmd) (Spring 2025), [**AI and Me**](Projects/AI_and_ME/AI_and_ME.qmd) (2025–present), and [**Teaching with Generative AI**](Teaching/Teaching%20with%20GenAI/Teaching%20with%20GenAI.qmd) (April 2024–present).

Previously, I was a researcher at **iFLYTEK's National Cognitive Intelligence Key Laboratory** (March 2021–June 2023), conducting mixed-method evaluations of smart-education initiatives and K–12 learning technologies. At **Shanghai Squirrel AI** (December 2017–August 2019), I worked as an instructor and adaptive learning specialist, using diagnostic data to personalize learning and supporting teachers' use of adaptive systems.

## Education

- **Ph.D., Learning Design and Technology**, University of Tennessee, Knoxville, August 2023–present. Committee: Joshua Rosenberg, Enilda Romero-Hall, Victor Lee, and Jason Johnston.
- **M.A., Education Technology**, Johnson University, 2020–2021.
- **M.S., Education Technology**, Anhui Normal University, 2019–2022.
- **B.S., Software Engineering**, Longyan University, 2012–2016.

## Service

I have served as a peer reviewer for the *Journal of Research on Technology in Education* (2024–2025), the *Journal of Statistics and Data Science Education* (2025), and AECT (2025), and as president of the University of Tennessee's CSSA student organization.

[View my full CV →](CV.qmd)

I believe in the motto: **"Technology comes and goes, pedagogy never falls."** This guides my work toward grounded, human-centered learning experiences.
